findings.name: Overused font
findings.description: Inter, Roboto, Fraunces, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, and Space Grotesk are used on so many sites they no longer feel distinctive. Each new wave of AI-generated UIs converges on the same handful of faces. Choose a face that gives your interface personality.

findings.name: Straggler
findings.description: The last line of this paragraph holds one word, which leaves a hole under the block. Set text-wrap: pretty on body copy (Chrome, Safari) to pull a word down beside it. Where a browser ignores it, edit the last sentence or bind the last two words with a no-break space. Keep it if the break is intended.
findings.snippet: "level." alone on the last of 2 lines (7% of the measure)

findings.name: Low contrast text
findings.description: Text does not meet WCAG AA contrast requirements (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text). Increase the contrast between text and background.

findings.name: Same text repeated inside one container
findings.description: The same literal text rendered three or more times in structurally different spots inside a single card or panel is redundant messaging — usually a status or label wired into every slot of a template. Say it once, in the slot where it matters most.
findings.snippet: "Required" rendered 3× in distinct spots inside article.lib-panel

findings.name: Em-dash overuse
findings.description: Em-dash saturation in body copy is an AI cadence tell. Advisory only: humans use em-dashes legitimately, so this fires only on saturation — at least 8 em-dashes (— or --) at a density near one per 500 characters of body text — never on a long article that uses a few. Prefer commas, colons, periods, or parentheses.

findings.name: Repeating-gradient stripes
findings.description: Repeating-gradient stripes used as surface decoration are a recurring generated-UI signature. Reach for a deliberate texture or leave the surface plain.

findings.name: Nested cards
findings.description: Cards inside cards create visual noise and excessive depth. Flatten the hierarchy — use spacing, typography, and dividers instead of nesting containers.
